what_it_does: This paper studies how well large language models (LLMs) tolerate hardware faults—bits flipping incorrectly in memory or computation during inference. While prior work claims LLMs are resilient to bit errors, this study reveals that standard metrics mask serious problems: the model's formal accuracy may stay high while the generated text becomes gibberish or semantically nonsensical. The paper injects random bit faults during inference and measures both traditional metrics and text quality.
